findings.what: The main door's broad outer pilaster stands in the wrong place. In the photo it stands on the raised platform, on a red-painted base block at the inner edge of the stone coping, in line with the bay post's passage-side face. Two or three stepped jamb members stand on the coping between it and the platform edge, and only the inner carved frame (rosette base, lintel with boss) goes down into the passage. In the model the pilaster stands in the lowered passage on a grey stone base, about 0.3 m short of the platform edge, with bare turquoise wall between it and the platform. veranda.jpg agrees: the window reveal is only about 0.4 m from the pilaster, where the model has about 1.3 m.

The model's 'Veranda carved transverse bracket' is a one-sided bracket only 1.24 m long, with a pointed pendant hanging about 0.55 m below the beam at mid-span. The pendant is visible in the render at upper centre.
findings.proposal: Redraw the bracket Shape (house.js 611-613). Remove the bezier control point at y -0.88 so nothing hangs below about -0.30. Make the transverse piece symmetric over the full bay depth (z 0.57 to 1.91, 1.34 m): end corbels 0.45 deep stepping up in three scallops of about 0.06 radius over 0.35 m, a soffit 0.15 below the beam, and a centre keel notch 0.15 wide by 0.08 high. Use the same pendant-free profile for 'Veranda scalloped carved beam bracket'.

In 14.58.02 the eave is ~10.3 m above the eye-level line through three standing men's heads at ~53 m, i.e. ~12 m above the forecourt. The earlier plinth raise to 2.8 m did not close the gap.

Stage figures become ~2.1 m. If the 20 m width is the less certain number, the alternative is narrowing to ~15 m (z -12.5..2.5) at current heights; the horizon evidence favours raising.

poseComment: The saved eye (-2.39, 2.17, -13.21) is over open water, 3.2 m beyond the lake rail, facing NNE to the far bank ~21 m away; the render shows the west/far corner with the far-bank stairs. The photo was taken 6 s after 14.57.50 (camera at x 9.8) and 6 s before 14.58.02 (x 6.7), so the photographer was at the lane-side rail near x ~8, holding the camera out over the rail and looking down WNW at a turtle. The corner at top-left is then the lane/west corner (-5, -10) about 13-14 m away (its depression angle gives 14-19 m), the top band is the west bank, and the left edge is the lane-side bank's ledges. Suggested re-alignment start: eye ~(8, 1.7, -10.5), forward ~(-0.80, -0.48, -0.36). No findings from this render.

Far content (Stage roof, Shop house, east bank, temple block) is within ~3% of frame. The near field is not: the photo's true horizon (three men's heads at 7, 38 and 45 m all at y ~0.47) is ~2.5 deg below the pose's, and the stepped pier is ~7.2 m away in the photo against 5.5 m to the model pier, so the camera was ~1.5 m further west (x ~5.2).

The model has two plain whitewashed 0.59 m piers with sloped caps at the mouth (x 12.35), a pierced rail run from 12.35 to 16.03, and a single white four-tier stepped pier 4 m further in at x 16.4. 14.28.15 puts the lane-side stepped pier 9.9 m from that camera, i.e. at x ~12.3.
